prs.request:
PR title: fix(acp): treat os.ErrClosed as an agent-exit pipe write error

PR description:
## Summary

- When an ACP agent exits, `exec.Cmd.Wait` closes the parent's `StdinPipe` before the monitor goroutine closes `sc.done`. A `Nudge` that lands in that window fails its write with `write |1: file already closed` (`os.ErrClosed`). `isPipeWriteError` only recognized `io.ErrClosedPipe` and `EPIPE`, so the race came back to the caller as `sending prompt to "<name>": write: write |1: file already closed` instead of the documented best-effort `nil`. We saw this after SIGINT killed an agent mid-session.
- Fix: `isPipeWriteError` now also matches `os.ErrClosed` via `errors.Is`, which also catches wrapped `*os.PathError`. The existing write-failure path then waits for `sc.done` and returns `nil` with its existing stderr line (`acp: nudge to %q skipped (agent exiting): ...`).
- The contract is unchanged: the message is dropped with a stderr line, and the session layer restarts the agent on the next submit. Non-pipe write errors still surface right away (`TestNudge_NonPipeErrorSurfacesImmediately` still passes).

**Stack:** independent. Based on `main`, no parent or child PR.
**Related PRs:** #6114 (ACP startup ownership) rewrites parts of `acp.go` Start/Nudge. This change is a one-line predicate edit in `isPipeWriteError` and should rebase trivially either way. Other in-flight ACP PRs (#5263, #4687, #4618, #6406, #6368) don't touch this helper.

## Testing

- [x] `go test ./internal/runtime/acp/ -count=1`
- [x] `go test ./internal/testpolicy/resourcecensus/` (no new exec or sleep in tests)
- [x] `go vet ./...`
- [x] pre-commit hook (lint-changed, generated docs check, vet)
- [x] pre-push `make test-fast-parallel`
- [x] `make bazel-sync` (only change: the new test file added to `internal/runtime/acp/BUILD.bazel`)
- [ ] `make check`: not run separately; the pre-push fast suite covers the unit tier
- [ ] `make test-integration`: not run; this changes error classification only and has no integration-visible behavior beyond the unit-tested `Nudge` path

Tests were written first and failed before the fix:
- `TestIsPipeWriteError`: table test covering `os.ErrClosed`, a wrapped `*os.PathError{Err: os.ErrClosed}`, `EPIPE`, wrapped `EPIPE`, `io.ErrClosedPipe`, an unrelated error, and nil.
- `TestNudge_ReturnsNilWhenStdinAlreadyClosedByWait`: uses a real `os.Pipe` whose write end is already closed, the state `Cmd.Wait` leaves the stdin pipe in. The test is deterministic (it waits on the observed write, not on time) and spawns no process. PR title: fix(pool): restore <template>-<beadID> runtime names without the vcjr9 leak

PR description:
**v1.5.0 release blocker (P0-7).**

## Problem
RC Gate Tier C `TestFreshInit_SlingSpawnsDefaultPoolWorker` and `TestFreshInit_ClaudeUnrestricted` fail (run 35927640679) at `test/acceptance/tier_c/fresh_install_spawn_test.go:184`: the default `claude` pool worker runs under the bare session name `claude` instead of `claude-<beadID>`. The `<beadID>` token in the name is there on purpose: it lets you look up the session bead from the runtime name.

## Root cause
#5372 (the fix for the ga-vcjr9 pod leak) changed how unaliased pool runtime names are derived. They now come from the slot identity instead of the bead ID:
- `derivePoolSessionIdentifiers` → `poolRuntimeSessionName`, persisted by `createPoolSessionBeadWithIdentifiers` (`cmd/gc/session_name_lookup.go`)
- the sync lane `finalizeCreatedSessionName` (`cmd/gc/session_beads.go:~2000`)

With that change a canonical singleton gets `claude`, and a transient slot gets `<slot>-pool`.

The leak itself needed two things together:
- **(a)** the box from a failed attempt outlived the close of its row. `commitStartFailure`, the lease-expired rollbacks, and the failed-create close all closed the row without ever touching the runtime.
- **(b)** the successor got a different name.

#5372 removed (b). This PR removes (a).

## Fix (approved design `design-P0-7-beadid`)
- **Naming.** Unaliased pools persist `PoolSessionName(template, beadID)` again, at both minting sites. The identity-derived name is still computed, locked, and availability-checked, but only as the slot's lease and lock identifier. tmux_alias pools and named sessions are unchanged.
- **Teardown before close, fail closed.** `releaseBeadScopedPoolRuntime` calls `sp.Stop(name)` before any close of an unconfirmed bead-scoped pool create. That covers:
  - `commitStartFailure`: the generic rollback arm and the terminal-provider-error arm
  - `attemptRollbackPendingCreate` (lease-expired and foreign-runtime rollbacks)
  - the reconciler's open failed-create close

  If the Stop fails, the row stays OPEN in its pending state and logs `holding pool session <id> open`. The slot stalls instead of leaking.
  - Stopping by name is always safe here, because the name embeds this row's own bead ID.
  - In the terminal arm the teardown now runs *before* `markProviderTerminalError`. Otherwise a held row would be parked asleep with its claim cleared, where no path retries the teardown. This fixes a gap in the prototype.
- **Identity lease.** `ensurePoolIdentityNotHeldByOpenRow` refuses to mint a successor while an open start-pending, creating, or failed-create row holds the same slot identity.
- **Quarantine key.** `startupHealthEpisodeKey` keys the #6016 startup-health episode on the stable pool identity, so the retry-storm quarantine still builds up across bead generations.
- **Comments and docs.** Stale comments that described identity-derived runtime names are updated.
- **Tier C.** The Tier C assertion is tightened from `claude-*` to exactly `claude-<beadID>`.

## Review round 1 (b20a081356)
- **Context-canceled commit.** The context-canceled rollback in `commitAsyncStartResultWithContext` is now gated by `releaseBeadScopedPoolRuntime`. A held row keeps its claim, so the lease-expired rollback retries the teardown.
- **Stale async start.** `stopStaleAsyncStartRuntime` now stops a bead-scoped pool runtime by name even when its GC_SESSION_ID / GC_INSTANCE_TOKEN attribution is unreadable. This covers an async Start that finishes after the lease-expired rollback has already closed the row.
  - It is not fully unconditional: a box that positively reports a different instance token is left alone. The same bead rotates its token on every wake, so that box belongs to a newer generation of the bead.
- **Legacy startup-health episode.** A successful start clears the legacy bare-identity episode. It is kept if any non-pool session, or a still-open one, ever carried that name.
- **Sync-lane mint.** The sync-lane pool mint (`syncSessionBeads`) now applies `ensurePoolIdentityNotHeldByOpenRow`. Production callers exist (city_runtime.go, cmd_start.go), so I could not prove it unreachable.

  - `TestCommitAsyncStart_StaleResultStopsUnattributedBeadScopedPoolRuntime` (with the newer-token control)
  - `TestReconcileSessionBeads_PoolSuccessClearsLegacyStartupHealthEpisode` (with the non-pool-holder control)
  - `TestSyncSessionBeads_PoolMintRespectsIdentityLease`

- New reconciler-level test `TestReconcileSessionBeads_PoolTeardownFailureHoldsUnconfirmedCreate`, covering the lease-expired rollback and the open failed-create close:
  - When Stop fails, the row stays open in its state for 3 ticks, with no Start and no successor bead.

prs.title: fix(session): fence ACP startup ownership and pending-create rollback
prs.author: Toady00
prs.request:
PR title: fix(session): fence ACP startup ownership and pending-create rollback

PR description:
## Summary

Fixes #6109.

ACP Start exposed a live startup sentinel before seeding the ownership sidecars read by GetMeta. Supplying identity through the child environment alone did not populate those files. Separately, pending-create rollback could close a successfully completed creation using a stale snapshot because its read and rollback transaction were not serialized with asynchronous completion.

- Seed only classified metadata before publishing the sentinel or control socket. Do not persist credentials from the child environment.
- Serialize ACP startup and cleanup by runtime name, retain ownership until failed startup cleanup drains, and preserve replacement runtimes and their sidecars.
- Interrupt backpressured handshake writes on cancellation or deadline. Disarm and join the cancellation callback before transferring the connection, and release the lifecycle lock before initial nudge delivery so Stop can interrupt it.
- Re-read the lease and commit completion or rollback under the existing process-local session mutation lock. Reject stale completion without emitting success, and clean up only the attempted runtime identity outside that lock.
- Defer fresh canonical singleton record allocation while its derived runtime name is occupied, rather than repeatedly minting failed records or adopting a foreign runtime.

The controller fence is process-local, not a cross-process store CAS. Direct external bead writes remain outside its guarantee. A still-claimed advisory awake state remains rollback-eligible when Start fails.

## Evidence and scope

The source defects and deterministic reproductions were confirmed against `6ba434271c5f76bc150f694ebeef9d713be16b3a`. The inspected incident contained 77 session records; one correlated record completed creation at relative t=0 and was closed as failed-create at t=+354ms. Local paths and identities are redacted.

The exact installed binary provenance for that incident is unknown. Current-source reproduction does not establish which commit produced the installed binary, and no live replay has been performed.

#2112 has the closest reported symptoms. #5436 concerns different routing behavior; #4714 and #5895 concern orphan cleanup; #6104 and PR #6105 concern a different recovery race. This PR does not claim to fix all of those reports.

## Verification

Completed on macOS arm64 with Go 1.26.6, resolved toolchain PATH, inherited GOROOT unset, and ICU build flags:

- `go test -race ./internal/runtime/acp ./internal/session -count=1` passed.
- `go test -race ./internal/runtime/acp -count=10` passed after the final lint fixes.
- `go test -race ./cmd/gc -run "Test(RollbackPendingCreate|StartCompletionRejects|FailedStartRollsBack|AsyncStartFinalCommit|SingletonPendingCreate|CommitStartResult|ReconcileSessionBeads_.*PendingCreate)" -count=10` passed.
- CLI build passed with output outside the checkout; nothing was installed or restarted.

## Confirmed defects

Source inspection and deterministic reproductions against main at `6ba434271c5f76bc150f694ebeef9d713be16b3a` confirm two interacting startup defects:

- ACP `Provider.Start` publishes an alive in-memory sentinel before the handshake, but does not seed the ownership sidecars used by `GetMeta`. Passing `GC_SESSION_ID`, `GC_INSTANCE_TOKEN`, and `GC_RUNTIME_EPOCH` to the child environment does not populate those sidecars. A reconciler can therefore see a live runtime without the identity needed to recognize its pending creation.
- Pending-create rollback checks only whether the bead is already closed before writing its rollback transaction. It does not atomically revalidate the pending claim and incarnation against asynchronous start completion. A stale creating snapshot can close a creation that has already completed, clear its explicit runtime name, and leave the runtime occupying that name.

For a canonical singleton, continuing demand can then allocate and retire more session records while that runtime remains alive. This report does not authorize adoption or termination of a foreign runtime.

PR title: fix(formulas): append work-bead notes instead of replacing them

PR description:
## Problem

Five core-pack formula steps pass `--notes` to `$WORK_BEAD_ID`. `bd update --notes` replaces the notes field, so each of these steps discards any notes the bead already carries. On 2026-09-15 one such write destroyed four coordinator notes on a live issue; the operator recovered them from `dolt_history_issues`, which worked only because someone noticed in time.

beads PR https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/6583 makes `bd update --notes` refuse the write when the target bead already holds different, non-empty notes. Once that lands, these five steps fail instead of clobbering. This change moves them to `--append-notes`, which preserves the history and already works with the current `bd`.

## Change

`--notes` becomes `--append-notes` at the five sites that target `$WORK_BEAD_ID`:

- `internal/bootstrap/packs/core/formulas/mol-do-work.toml` (the shipped close and the no-op close)
- `internal/bootstrap/packs/core/formulas/mol-polecat-commit.toml`
- `internal/bootstrap/packs/core/formulas/mol-polecat-report.toml`
- `internal/bootstrap/packs/core/formulas/mol-prompt-synth.toml`

`mol-do-work.toml` keeps `--notes` for `$GC_BEAD_ID` and `$DRAIN_BEAD_ID`, because a step wisp and a drain bead hold no prior notes.

`TestCoreMolPolecatReportWriteReportStepRecordsNoteAndAvoidsPRFlow` pinned the literal substring `--notes`, which `--append-notes` does not contain, so the expected substring moves with the flag. The assertion's intent is unchanged: the step records the report on the work bead.

`internal/bdflags/bdflags.go` already lists `--append-notes` as a value flag for `bd update`, so `gc bd` forwards it today with no other change.

## Verification

PR title: fix(bd): ignore a stale or relative ambient BD_BIN instead of failing closed

PR description:
**v1.5.0 release blocker** (bead ga-weekw).

## Problem
An inherited `BD_BIN` that is relative (`bd`, `./bin/bd`) or no longer executable (e.g. a removed `/opt/beads/bd-rc2` still exported by a long-lived shell) takes a managed city offline. Every `gc bd` call, `gc doctor`, the store-open preflight (`requireBdBinaryForCity`), managed bd env composition, controller/provider subprocess env and the provider lifecycle all fail with `ambient BD_BIN "..." must be an absolute executable path` / `... is not executable`. Workaround: `unset BD_BIN`. This is a regression since v1.4.2, introduced by #5421.

## Root cause
- `cmd/gc/bd_env.go:194-201` (`workspacePinnedBdBinaryOptional`, ambient branch): a relative or non-executable ambient BD_BIN returns an error. At the city scope `resolveBdBinaryForScope` always consults the pin, so the error reaches every caller.
- `cmd/gc/bd_env.go:2089` (`applyWorkspacePinnedBdBinary`): BD_BIN is written only when a pin exists, so a stale *absolute* inherited value survives in the child base env. `internal/beads/bdstore.go` `execCommandRunner` then execs it (`fork/exec /nonexistent/bin/bd: no such file or directory`).

## Fix (option A from the release validation)
- Ambient branch: a relative or non-executable ambient BD_BIN resolves as "no pin" and prints one stderr line per process naming the ignored value (`gc: warning: ignoring ambient BD_BIN "..." (not executable); using bd from PATH`). The line is deduped per value because one process resolves the pin several times.
- `applyWorkspacePinnedBdBinary` always writes `BD_BIN`, empty when there is no pin. The empty value masks the stale inherited one, so the exec runner falls back to PATH. The lifecycle scripts use `${BD_BIN:-bd}`, and the bound-store runner already writes an empty BD_BIN.
- **Unchanged:** a declared `workspace.env` BD_BIN that is invalid, and a `workspace.env` PATH with no bd, still fail closed.
- **Deliberately not shipped:** the bead's `resolvePin` swap. Testing showed it doesn't fix this bug (the error comes from the Optional resolver). It also silently weakens the "workspace PATH has no bd" guard.

## Tests (fail before, pass after)
- `TestAmbientInvalidBdBinIsIgnoredNotFatal` (ambient `bd`, `./bin/bd`, `/nonexistent/bin/bd`):
  - `resolveBdBinaryForScope`, `requireBdBinaryForCity` and `applyWorkspacePinnedBdBinary` succeed.
  - `env[BD_BIN]` is present and empty.
  - The exec runner runs the PATH bd.
  - Exactly one warning line names the value.
  - **Before:** all 3 subtests fail with `ambient BD_BIN "bd" must be an absolute executable path` / `... is not executable`.
- `TestGcBdPassthroughIgnoresStaleAmbientBdBin`: `gc bd update` end to end with a stale absolute BD_BIN.
  - **Before:** `doBd() = 1`, `gc bd: ambient BD_BIN "/nonexistent/beads/bd-rc2" is not executable`.
- `TestWorkspacePathWithoutBdStillFailsClosedWithValidAmbientBdBin` and `TestInvalidWorkspaceBdBinStillFailsClosed`: guards that pass before and after, and pin the fail-closed behavior for declared pins.
- `TestOrderExecEnvReservedKeysCoverProjectedEnv`: BD_BIN is now always projected into the order exec env, so the test exempts it explicitly.
  - It was already projected (and not reserved) whenever a pin was configured, and `[order.env] BD_BIN` could already override it.
  - This PR keeps that behavior rather than newly rejecting orders that set BD_BIN.
- Local runs: full `go test ./cmd/gc` passes; `go vet` and gofmt are clean.

## Risks
- A deliberately exported but mistyped ambient BD_BIN now silently gets the PATH bd. The stderr warning mitigates this.
- Child processes now see `BD_BIN=` (empty) instead of the inherited value when no pin exists. The in-tree consumers use `${BD_BIN:-bd}` / `[ -n "${BD_BIN:-}" ]`.
- No config shape change and no upgrade impact.

Behind `GC_BEADS_PROXIED_NATIVE=1`, **default off**: with the flag off, direct and hosted cities behave byte-identically to main (error identity, call counts, reopen counts, elapsed), pinned by tests.

## What it does

With the flag on, a proxied-server scope serves **reads** natively through the beads library over bd's db-proxy, instead of forking the bd CLI per read. **Writes stay on the bd CLI.** bd remains the lifecycle owner: gc never spawns dolt or the proxy, and recovery runs only through the provider script's sanctioned verbs (`bd ping`, and `recover` = `bd dolt stop` + `bd ping`), at most one `bd dolt stop` per proxy generation per process.

- **Admission.** An unforgeable pin is minted only after the probe session proves the proxy's identity (proxy.pid, root id, birth) and the schema cursors. The ignored lane is compared on the *effective* cursor, the same clamped number beads' own migrate check uses. A reality the production probe did not evaluate is refused. The library therefore cannot migrate bd's schema from a handle gc opened to read.
- **Post-open check.** HEAD and the ignored-plane sentinel reality are re-read on one pinned connection after the open. A move refuses the open loudly (`proxied_native_head_moved`, WARN, at every producing site).
- **Classification.** Typed read errors (indeterminate commit, circuit open, 1049, 1045, connection level) are gated on the lane. A probe whose own clock ran out is never a verdict. One probe is exactly one proxy session.
- **Lifecycle.** A 15s guard tick re-pins on a new proxy generation, holds recovery to one probe session per tick, and stands down only on terminal verdicts. Draining is a bounded wait. The zombie ladder (SIGTERM'd dolt child) spends exactly one `bd dolt stop`. A rig sharing the city's proxy root leaves recovery to the city.
- **Read/write split.** A `ProxiedStore` wrapper bounds every read-your-own-write hazard in the plan's register. It deliberately claims no native write capability; `readOnlyReason` fences 19 mutators, and doctor sees post-open demotion.
- **Observability.** The `gc doctor --json` beads-store payload carries the proxied verdict, generation and endpoint.

| command | flag off | flag on |
|---|---|---|
| `gc status --json` | 8 bd forks, 1.89s | **0 forks, 0 pings, 0.75s** |
| `gc doctor --json` | 107 forks | **3 forks** |

PR description:
Fixes #6316.

## What changed

`doltServerEnv` now strips the per-session identity keys before the environment reaches the managed Dolt scope watchdog and the `dolt sql-server` beneath it. The set is what `session.RuntimeEnvWithSessionContext` injects into an agent runtime (`GC_SESSION_ID`, `GC_SESSION_NAME`, `GC_ALIAS`, `GC_AGENT`, `GC_TEMPLATE`, `GC_SESSION_ORIGIN`, `GC_RUNTIME_EPOCH`, `GC_CONTINUATION_EPOCH`, `GC_INSTANCE_TOKEN`, `BEADS_HOLDER_TOKEN`, `BEADS_ACTOR`) plus `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`. `startManagedDoltSQLServerWithScopeWatchdog` gains an env-taking inner variant so a test can spawn the real watchdog under a stamped environment without mutating its own.

## Why

A `gc dolt restart` (or any auto-ensure start) from inside an agent session left the watchdog carrying that session's `GC_SESSION_ID`. The watchdog reparents to init, so `sweepProcessTableOrphans` reported it as the session's process-table root and terminated it once the session bead closed; the watchdog's SIGTERM handler then terminated the server. On one city this took Dolt down twice in eleven minutes, each time about 15 seconds after an agent session exited, with the controller's circuit breaker open in between. PR description:
**v1.5.0 release blocker.** This fixes the top cause of red `main` CI and unblocks the required `cmd/gc process` shard on every v1.5.0 backport PR. It is first in the backport queue.

## Problem
`TestGcBeadsBdProviderOwnedRealLifecycleStopsOwnedProcesses/proxied` fails intermittently with `beads_provider_lifecycle_test.go:13099: provider-owned process N remained alive after stop`. It failed 6 of the last 8 `main` runs. The failure is in the test, not the product: `gc stop` does stop the processes.

## Root cause
- `cmd/gc/beads_provider_lifecycle_test.go:13097-13100` checks each published pid once, immediately after `run(ctx, "stop")`, with `processStillAlive` (`cmd/gc/path_helpers_test.go:561`). That probe is `kill(pid, 0)`, which also succeeds on zombies.
- On the proxied path, `bd dolt stop` (`proxy.Shutdown`) first SIGKILLs the db-proxy, then the Dolt backend. bd reports the stop once every recorded process is gone **or a zombie**: `procid` treats state `Z`/`X` as exited.
- The backend is the killed proxy's child, so it is reparented to PID 1 and stays a zombie until init reaps it. The test's one-shot probe runs inside that window.
- Repro on a loaded host: 32 of 48 proxied runs failed. Every failure was `"<pid> (dolt) Z 1 ..."`, and each of those pids was gone 14-26 ms later.

## Fix (test-only, one file)
Replace the one-shot `kill(pid, 0)` check with the zombie-aware `pidAlive` probe (`pidutil.Alive`, which counts `Z` as dead, the same rule bd uses), polled against a 5s deadline by a new helper, `waitForProviderOwnedPIDStopped`.
- The helper polls on a context-aware ticker rather than `time.Sleep`, so the untagged `fixed_sleep` census ratchet does not grow.
- On timeout it fails with the pid's last observed `/proc/<pid>/stat` state, as TESTING.md requires for black-box polling.
- The short poll is still needed: bd returns as soon as the proxy's flock is released, and for a brief window before that the proxy is neither a zombie nor gone.
- A process that really survives stop is still alive at the deadline, so real leaks still fail the test.

## Tests
- **Before (instrumented, 4×12 proxied):** 32/48 FAIL, each on a zombie dolt backend with ppid 1.
- **After:** 96/96 PASS (4×12, direct + proxied).
- **Negative control:** with `stop` removed and the fix in place, the test fails with `provider-owned process N remained alive 5s after stop; last state: N (bd) S 1 ...`.
- **This branch:** `GC_FAST_UNIT=0 go test ./cmd/gc -run TestGcBeadsBdProviderOwnedRealLifecycleStopsOwnedProcesses -count=5` gives 10/10 subtests PASS on the first commit and 6/6 on the ticker version.
- **Checks:** `go test ./cmd/gc -count=1` and `go test ./internal/testpolicy/...` pass, and `gofmt` and `go vet ./cmd/gc` are clean.

- **Product code:** none; one assertion changes.
- **`processStillAlive`:** left unchanged. It is still used by the `reapDoltLeakPIDs` cleanup, where the same zombie blind spot only costs a bounded wait.
- **macOS:** `pidutil.Alive` falls back to `ps` for zombie detection, and the poll still bounds the wait.

   detaches the memo, and it runs only from the per-invocation CLI entry
   (`cmd/gc/main.go:181`). Nothing reopens a route it finds closed.

4. Every later funnel consumer in the process therefore gets `ErrStoreClosed`
   (`internal/beads/sqlite_store.go:499-505`) — nudge delivery itself, and the
   controller's `session-circuit-reset` socket handler, which reaches the funnel through
   `handleSessionCircuitResetSocketCmd` (`cmd/gc/controller.go:265`) →
   `cliSessionStore` → `cliStorageRoutes`.

`cmd/gc/cmd_order.go:2126` is **not** affected: it closes the raw work store it opened,
with no class resolver in between.

## What it looks like in production

A managed city with the supported whole-infrastructure split (`graph`/`sessions`/
`messaging`/`orders`/`nudges` → one `sqlite-beads` binding). 1h45m into a controller run,
both of these went dead together and stayed dead for the next 7.6 hours, through many
healthy reconcile ticks:

- supervisor-side nudge delivery, and
- `gc session reset <named-session>`, which aborts at its circuit-breaker clear:

```
gc session reset: clearing session circuit breaker for "mayor": loading session circuit
breaker metadata for gcg-502: sqlite store: bead store closed
```

Side-effect-free probe against a live controller (the handler's first act on that path is
a read):

```
$ printf 'session-circuit-reset:{"identity":"probe","session_id":"gcg-000000"}\n' | nc -U .gc/controller.sock
{"outcome":"failed","error":"loading session circuit breaker metadata for gcg-000000: sqlite store: bead store closed"}
```

Healthy controller: a not-found error for `gcg-000000`.

This is the underlying condition behind #5973 (which reports the separate, independent
defect that `gc session reset` treats that failure as fatal and never reaches
`handle.Reset`). The two are complementary: this one is why the clear fails; #5973 is why
the failure costs you the whole reset.

## Reproducer

`cmd/gc` test on the repo's own `migratedOneShotCLICity` fixture: build a converged split
city, read the sessions class through the routes (healthy), run one nudge maintenance
frame, read again.

Before the fix, on `f07cfb682`:

```
--- FAIL: TestNudgeMaintenanceFrameLeavesTheStorageRoutesServingALiveStore (0.15s)
    nudge_store_ownership_test.go:43: the nudge maintenance frame closed the storage
    routes' shared engine; the routes still serve it and every later class read fails:
    sqlite store: bead store closed
```

After: PASS. The test ships with the PR.

## Fix candidates

**A — close only what the frame opened (the PR).** Give the nudges frames a close half that
declines to close a handle the routes own (`closeOwnedNudgeStore`), and skip the open whose
result `resolveNudgesStore` would only discard. Small, local to `cmd/gc/nudge_beads.go` +
the three `cmd_nudge.go` close sites, and it also stops the per-frame leak of the work
store on relocated cities.

**B — make the ownership un-loseable in the resolver.** Have `resolveClassStore` return an
explicit ownership token (or a no-op closer) alongside the store, so no caller can hold a
borrowed handle that looks like an owned one. Bigger, and it would retire this whole class
of bug rather than this instance — there are ~21 direct `cliStorageRoutes` call sites and
`residency_topology.go:96-105` already warns that the funnel is the wrong side of the
controller boundary.

I've sent A. Happy to follow with B if you want the resolver contract tightened.

## Prior art

#3157 (closed) is the same family one class-resolver earlier: a per-tick close of a store
the closer did not exclusively own, producing `bead store closed` on a native-Dolt city.

`gc ready` (the agent work query) loaded the full city config once per bound rig, even though the command had already loaded it. The rig-leg opener called `openStoreAtForCity`, which hands `openStoreResultAtForCityWithConfig` a nil cfg and forces a reload. This threads the command's own config into **one-shot** store opens only. The long-lived controller, supervisor, order dispatcher and API paths keep reloading per open, because their freshness comes from the config.Revision reload path, and some of them pass an empty stand-in cfg.

A process-wide memo inside `loadCityConfig` was considered and rejected. Callers mutate the returned `*config.City` (for example `resolveRigPaths` rewrites rig paths in place). Stat-validating `Provenance.Sources` does not cover imported pack directories. And nothing marks a process as one-shot.

- `openStandaloneRigStores` takes a `rigStoreOpener`. Controller callers pass the reloading `openStoreAtForCity`, unchanged.
- `oneShotRigStoreOpener(cfg)`, `buildStandaloneRigStoresWithConfig` and `openCityStoreAtWithConfig` are used by `cmdReady` and `readyRigLegStores`.

- `gc session close`, drain-ack and the `gc hook --claim` fence.
- A one-shot bd city-scope open (`openOneShotBdStoreAtWithConfig`), threaded as an explicit `oneShotConfig` flag.

prs.title: fix(runtime): keep secret SetMeta values out of tmux argv
prs.author: julianknutsen
prs.request:
PR title: fix(runtime): keep secret SetMeta values out of tmux argv

PR description:
## Summary

A security review on a shared host found Manifold API keys in agent tool results, captured from `ps` / `/proc/*/cmdline` output of `tmux new-session -e ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=…`. The line the review cited (`tmux.go:473`) comes from a stale 2026-07-21 checkout. On `main`, #5425 (2026-08-19) already stages secret `new-session` env through a private 0600 command file, using an **allow-list** (`runtime.envArgvSafe`), so any key not on the list is treated as secret. The deployed release binary includes that fix.

This PR closes the argv paths that #5425 did not cover:

- **Local tmux `SetEnvironment` (the `SetMeta` backend)** still ran `tmux set-environment -t S KEY VALUE` with the value in argv. Now any value that `runtime.ArgvSecretEnvValue` classifies as secret goes through the same private command file (`runFromCommandFile`, factored out of `runNewSession`). If the file can't be staged, the call fails closed. Inert values stay on argv, so the common identity and epoch writes create no files.
- **ssh provider `SetMeta`** put the value in argv on the box *and* in the local ssh client's argv, because the remote command is folded into one argument. Secret values are now staged on the box over stdin, reusing `stageSecretEnv`, and applied with `source-file`. `SetMeta` stays best-effort, but a staging failure skips the write rather than falling back to argv.

## Tests
- `TestNoSecretEnvValueReachesAnyTmuxArgv`: property test. No non-allowlisted value (credentials, `GC_INSTANCE_TOKEN`, a future unknown key, a hostile value with quotes/`$`/`#{}`/newline) appears in any tmux argv across `NewSessionWithCommandAndEnv` + `SetEnvironment`, and no staged dir is left behind.
- tmux: staged-mechanism, inert-path and fail-closed tests for `SetEnvironment`.
- ssh: secret-off-argv, fail-without-fallback and inert-path tests for `SetMeta`.
- The integration test `TestSecretEnvIsAbsentFromProcCmdline` (real tmux 3.4) now also sets a hostile value twice, once through the argv path and once through the staged path, and checks that tmux reads back the same thing both times. `show-environment` re-escapes `$`, so byte-equality with the input is not the right check.
- I confirmed the new unit tests fail without the fix.

Local gates: `make fmt-check`, `make lint-changed` (0 issues), `make vet`, `go test ./internal/runtime/... ./internal/session/...`, `go test -tags integration ./internal/runtime/tmux/`, `GC_FAST_UNIT=0 go test ./cmd/gc -run 'Drain|Meta|Restart|InstanceToken'`. One unrelated `proctable` setsid test flaked once; it passes 5/5 on rerun and does not depend on these packages.

## Remaining argv exposures (not changed here)
- `scripts/gc-session-docker` (exec provider) passes **all** session env as `docker run -e K=V`, `docker exec -e K=V` (pre_start/setup) and `tmux new-session -e K=V` via `docker exec`, all in host argv. Suggested fix: `docker run/exec -e NAME` with the value in the docker CLI's own environment, or `--env-file` with a 0600 file for single-line values; drop the redundant tmux `-e` because `docker exec` inherits the container env.
- herdr: `workspace create` / `tab create` pass env as `--env K=V` to the herdr CLI. This is already documented in `herdr/redaction.go` as needing a private env channel in herdr itself.
- k8s: `SetMeta` runs `tmux set-environment` through client-go exec. That is argv inside the pod only, not on the controller host; low severity.

prs.title: fix(dispatch): stop passing retry attempts from aborting their scope
prs.author: sjarmak
prs.request:
PR title: fix(dispatch): stop passing retry attempts from aborting their scope

PR description:
## Summary

A retry attempt that closes with a passing result can still abort its enclosing scope or fail its workflow. Two bugs in `internal/dispatch` combine to cause it, and this PR fixes both.

1. **Attach-created attempts never get `gc.logical_bead_id`.** `buildAttemptRecipe` stamps `gc.control_for` on a spawned retry or Ralph attempt root, but not `gc.logical_bead_id`. `isRetryAttemptSubject` therefore never recognizes the attempt as retry-managed, and when a later attempt bare-closes with a typed deliverable disposition, `beadOutcomeFailed` reads it as a terminal `abort_scope` failure. That happens at two sites: `processScopeCheck` and the `processWorkflowFinalize` terminal-failure scan. The fix stamps `gc.logical_bead_id = control.ID` next to `gc.control_for`, matching what `retryAttemptBead` already does on the v1 path. It covers simple retry, nested retry and Ralph iterations through the shared constructor.

2. **`beadOutcomeFailed` checks `gc.outcome=fail` before the retry-attempt exemption.** A retry attempt that failed was reported as a terminal `on_fail=abort_scope` failure before the retry controller had a chance to act. For any step carrying `on_fail=abort_scope`, that made retries inert. The check now applies the exemption first. All three abort-scope decision sites (`processScopeCheck`, `reconcileTerminalScopedMember`, `terminalAbortScopeFailure`) delegate to this predicate, so they now agree. A bead that is not a retry attempt and has `gc.outcome=fail` still fails closed, and the superseded-attempt exclusion from #4008 is unchanged.

We observed this on a live deployment: retry attempts that passed still failed their workflow, so every retry held a worker slot and bought nothing.

## Test plan

- New regression test drives attempt creation through the real `processRetryControl -> spawnNextAttempt -> molecule.Attach` path instead of hand-built beads (the existing `terminalAbortScopeFailure` tests build beads by hand, which is why they missed this), then exercises both false-abort sites end to end.
- `TestBeadOutcomeFailedConvergesAcrossAbortScopeDecisionSites` checks that all three decision sites agree for four cases: a retry attempt with an explicit fail, a non-retry bead with an explicit fail, a transient attempt failure, and a superseded attempt. `TestReconcileTerminalScopedMemberRetryAttemptExplicitFailDoesNotAbortScope` covers the reconcile path.
- Design note: `engdocs/design/abort-scope-retry-attempt-exemption-ordering.md`, registered in `engdocs/design/index.md`.
- `make build`, `go vet ./...`, `make test` and `make check-docs` pass at this head.

prs.title: fix(convergence): stop reclassifying genuine gate verdicts as blind reads (post-merge #6341)
prs.author: julianknutsen

PR title: fix(convergence): stop reclassifying genuine gate verdicts as blind reads (post-merge #6341)

PR description:
Post-merge review remediation for #6341 (landed range `88639e5949..c41c5cfa07`).
That PR fixed the ga-pqlgh root cause correctly; this follow-up fixes defects the
post-merge audit found in the fix itself. No behaviour from #6341 is reverted.

## The main one: overbroad blind-read markers

`gateInfraMarkers` (`internal/convergence/gate_infra.go`) is the stderr fallback
under the exit-75 protocol. A match tells the ralph dispatcher "this gate never
produced a verdict" and buys an attempt-free re-run, bounded by the shared
`maxCheckInfraRetries` budget of 20.

Two of the six entries matched on paths where the read did **not** fail:

- **`native_store_unavailable`** is logged on a *recovered* path. Every
  `logNativeUnavailable` call in `internal/beads/factory.go` (lines 161, 172,
  185, 198, 203, 214, 225) is immediately followed by `return
  opts.openBdFallback(...)` — the read succeeds. In any native-ineligible
  deployment (`GC_BEADS_FORCE_FALLBACK=1`, foreign `.beads/hooks`, a
  non-bd-contract provider, `preflight_unavailable`) it prints on every
  store-open. So the *first genuine* gate failure in such a city matched the
  marker, spent all 20 retries at ~15s cadence (~5 minutes of dead time with no
  agent working) and — because `cloneMetadata` carries the counter into later
  attempts — left a later real transport outage to burn semantic attempts
  instead. That is the exact incident shape the budget exists to prevent.
- **`gc import install`** is a remediation substring, not a typed error. It is
  the generic `RepairHint` in `internal/config/pack_include.go`,
  `internal/packman/check.go` and `cmd/gc/suggest.go` (including on the
  "agent name is wrong" path), and it is `cmd/gc/cmd_import.go`'s own error
  prefix — so a genuine `gc import install` failure tripped it. The typed
  pack-cache blindness it stood in for is already covered by the adjacent
  `locked but not cached` entry, which stays.

Both are dropped. `locked but not cached`, `no gc_home available`, `error 1045`
and `access denied for user` are kept — including the two that are the actual
ga-pqlgh signature.

The doc comment claimed "every entry is a typed error our own stack emits",
which was true of both dropped entries and still didn't make them safe. It now
states the admission rule that was missing: an entry must be a typed error
**and** must only appear when the read actually failed.

### Pack-cache coverage decision

The review left this open: rely on `locked but not cached`, or export a typed
token from `packman`/`config`. Taking the first — `locked but not cached` is
already the typed failure, and `gc import install` only ever shadowed it. No new
exported surface.

## Also fixed

- **`gate-sandbox-reads` could assert a control that did not pass.** It
  registered on `storeOK`, but `isBeadStoreUnreachable` deliberately excludes
  missing/uninitialized stores, and the `gc start` warmup path skips the probe
  entirely. In both shapes the check still printed "the same read succeeded for
  the controller" when no control had run — pointing the operator at a sandbox
  threading problem that is really a store-shape problem. It now registers only
  when the preflight actually ran and returned nil.
- **The probe's details/FixHint named four keys as if they were the whole env
  delta.** The controller's read is built by
  `bdRuntimeEnvWithErrorRecoveryContext`, which adds a workspace-pinned `BD_BIN`
  and the hosted credential passthrough; `ConditionEnv.Environ` threads none of
  them. A blind result now also lists the controller-only keys absent from the
  gate env, computed from `hostedBeadsCredentialPassthroughKeys` rather than
  hand-listed. The healthy branch stays quiet — nine absent key names on a
  passing check would be noise.
- **The ExactEnv runner was unpinned.** `defaultGateSandboxRead` inlined
  `beads.ExecCommandRunnerWithExactEnvContext`. Reverting it to a layering
  variant — the regression its own comment calls load-bearing — was invisible to
  the suite, because every test injects `probe`. Extracted to a package-level
  var with a sibling pin test, mirroring `TestHookClaimRunnerIsTheExactEnvRunner`.
- **`doctorClipGateOutput` could emit invalid UTF-8.** It sliced `out[:300]` on a
  byte boundary. It now backs up to a rune boundary.
- **Exit 75 was undocumented and its scope overstated.** A case-insensitive grep
  for `exit 75` / `EX_TEMPFAIL` / `tempfail` across `docs/` returned nothing, yet
  it is the protocol gate authors are meant to opt into — leaving the stderr
  marker table as the de-facto mechanism. And #6341's commit message stated
  "blind reads are attempt-free GateError" unconditionally, while
  `ClassifyInfraBlind` is applied only at `internal/dispatch/ralph.go:77-81`;
  trigger conditions, hybrid dispatch and `gc converge` still read a blind gate
  as a genuine verdict. Both are now specified in `formula-spec-v2.md` §3.1,
  with the lane scope stated explicitly.

The classifier rows that pinned the two dropped markers as blind are now
negative controls, and `internal/dispatch` grows a verdict-gate table asserting
those same two shapes still burn a semantic attempt and never touch the infra
budget — so the fix is guarded at both the unit and the dispatch level. Rows that
used `native_store_unavailable` merely as a payload (passing-gate, already-infra,
stdout-only) were switched to a still-live marker so they did not silently go
vacuous.

New doctor tests cover both non-registration shapes (non-outage preflight
failure, preflight skipped), the runner pin, the controller-only key
attribution on the blind branch and its absence on the healthy branch, and
`doctorClipGateOutput` (empty / short / long-ASCII / multibyte-across-the-cut).

prs.title: fix(reconciler): bound a pool slot stuck in drain so its name is released
prs.author: julianknutsen
prs.request:
PR title: fix(reconciler): bound a pool slot stuck in drain so its name is released

PR description:
## Summary

A pool-managed session bead that enters drain and cannot finalize its drain-ack stays `status=open` **forever**, and an open bead owns its `session_name`. Because a pool slot's name is deliberately a pure function of its identity (ga-vcjr9), the pool cannot route around it: it mints **zero** seats, and every bead routed to that template becomes unclaimable.

Production: bead `gcg-5436965277275192` held `beads--gc__implementation-worker-1-pool` open for **3 days 10 hours**, which starved PR #6119's ready worktree step and stalled the beads v1.3.0 rc.2 release for three days. The affected city had 6–8 such beads at diagnosis. The existing drain-ack deadline releases the *obligation*, not the bead — nothing bounded the state.

**Fix:** for pool-managed beads only, once the drain is past `poolSlotDrainRetireDeadline` (30m) and unfinalized, with **no assigned work** and a runtime proven absent (or stopped and re-observed absent), force `ClosePatch(now, "drained")` with greppable provenance and a counted typed event. Four ordered gates, all fail-closed; the kill is token-fenced.

## Two corrections the implementation made to its own design

- **The stuck seat does not stay in a drain state.** The reconciler re-heals a drained bead with a live runtime back to `state=awake`, so a state-name test would have missed nearly every real instance; the durable shape is `sleep_reason=drained` + empty `last_woke_at`. Measured on mainline: the shape survives **15 ticks with zero stop attempts**.
- **`drain_at` is never cleared**, so its age alone proves nothing — a seat whose drain was *cancelled* keeps an old `drain_at` while working normally. `sessionInUnfinalizedDrain` separates them on two independent markers, with a dedicated pin for that false-positive class.

## Review

Adversarial review returned 8 findings (4 major), all fixed. The decisive one: gate 3 originally resolved work-ownership through a narrow identifier set that omits `alias`/`alias_history`, while agents claim under their alias and `AssigneeIdentifier` resolves **alias-first** — and alias diverges from `session_name` exactly on the `-pool` step-aside shape, i.e. this bug's own specimen. A reviewer probe confirmed HEAD killed a live runtime and stranded its claim where base did not; gate 3 now uses the canonical `session.AssigneeIdentities` set. Also fixed: a leaked worktree per retirement, a close that skipped the partial-store and boot-deferral gates, overriding `held_until`/`quarantined_until`/`wait_hold`/`pin_awake`, a kill that was not re-fenced against work claimed mid-sequence, provenance that could outlive a refused close, and a stop invisible to the stop event and counter.

One finding was answered with evidence rather than applied: the `state=draining` arm was dead code, but relocating the gate would have bought **zero** retirements (that population converges in 3 ticks on its own) and reintroduced the shape §3.5 rejects — closing over a live agent. The dead arm was deleted and the boundary pinned instead.

## Problem

Graph.v2 route binding pre-stamped a **single-session config agent's** step `Assignee` with the **munged tmux runtime session name** — `SanitizeQualifiedNameForSession` turns `gascity-packs/gc.run-operator` into `gascity-packs--gc__run-operator` (`/`→`--`, `.`→`__`).

That's a category error. **`Assignee` is a unique reference to a concrete session**; an agent / config alias is a *routing* target. Config-agent work is delivered by **`gc.routed_to`** (the alias), and `Assignee` must stay empty until a session claims the step and stamps its own id — which is exactly what the pool lane already does. Stamping an agent-shaped value at cook time:

- matched no identity in the hook claim set (`hookClaimHasIdentity`), the controller's named-session wake-demand set, or the dead-assignee reaper's set — all keyed on concrete session identities — so the step could never be claimed *or* reopened; and

prs.author: julianknutsen
prs.request:
PR title: fix(session): give drain-ack stop-pending a terminal exit — escalate wedged seats to a fenced, subreaper-aware force-termination

PR description:
## Summary

A seat in `state=draining` / `state_reason=drain-ack-stop-pending` whose agent acknowledges the drain but whose **runtime survives the stop** has no exit: `finalizeDrainAckStopPendingSessions` only closes a row when the runtime observes dead, and while `obs.Running || obs.Alive` it reminds and re-queues forever — its own comment concedes the only historical exit is "an operator killing the pane". Because an OPEN bead owns its `session_name`, each wedged seat also permanently holds a pool slot name, so pools report `session name unavailable` and cannot mint replacements. Production: 7→16 seats wedged for 2+ days on one city, ~100 ready steps undispatched, 62 session rows stuck pending.

Two prior non-fixes are documented in the commits: the reminder budget is **suppressed** for agent-acked panes (the ack pin skips before any marker write, so a budget-only gate never fires for exactly the incident population), and `worker.Handle.Kill` is `Stop` minus the bead write — the same signal that already failed (tmux's terminate path discards kill errors and never re-observes; filed separately).

## The fix

**P0** — a two-arm terminal escalation (reminder-budget arm for askable seats; a `drain_at`-bounded arm for agent-acked seats), running **off-tick** with durable fail-closed pacing, that routes to `runtime.ProcessTableScanner` PID-level termination and falls through to the existing close terminus (one close path). The kill is fenced five ways: wide assignee-identity set (alias + alias_history), instance-token fence, positive runtime-binding attribution, attach/recent-activity holds, per-wave PID re-validation. **Attribution never trusts session-ID + city alone** — `GC_SESSION_ID` is inherited by every child the agent ever spawned, and the traced counterexample (the managed-Dolt scope watchdog, whose SIGTERM handler stops the city's *shared* dolt server) is a mandatory negative pin at **both** reparent topologies: init *and* the `systemd --user` child-subreaper this fleet actually runs (`internal/pidutil.IsReparentedOrphan`, extracted from the model `workspacesvc` already had). The scan-layer envelope exclusion is pinned separately in proctable.

**P1** — city stop/restart no longer chokes on draining seats: a distinct shutdown-intent seam (`SessionHandle.StopForShutdown` / `Manager.SuspendForShutdown`) used only by the shutdown sweep; targeted operator `suspend` keeps returning the illegal transition, and teardown errors propagate.

Events report **outcomes, not decisions** (killed / skipped-attribution / nothing-found), so "nothing reachable to kill" — the condition this pass exists to surface — is distinguishable from success.

## Review

Design → implementation → three adversarial review rounds + one focused coupling check: **4 criticals, 8 majors, 5 minors — all fixed**, including: the escalation being unreachable for the exact agent-acked population it was written for (the test fixture was green on the population's complement); "certified kill" not existing as a mechanism; the kill set sweeping in every env-inheriting descendant (the Dolt-watchdog shape); the shutdown latitude leaking to operator paths; and the `PPID <= 1` reparent test being blind to the subreaper topology. Every kill-safety invariant is mutation-pinned — each listed mutation fails exactly its own pin.

prs.title: fix(orders): dispatch due condition-triggered orders outside the per-tick rotation budget
prs.author: julianknutsen
prs.request:
PR title: fix(orders): dispatch due condition-triggered orders outside the per-tick rotation budget

PR description:
## The defect

`orders.max_dispatches_per_tick` (default 4) rationed **every** trigger type and
advanced its rotation cursor (`nextDispatchStart`) only when it spent a slot. So
each tick fired the first 4 due orders after the cursor and every order got a
dispatch opportunity roughly once per `ceil(orders / budget)` ticks.

That is the right shape for maintenance sweeps. It is the wrong shape for a
condition-triggered order, whose check does not say "I would like a turn" — it
says **work is pending right now**, and it says it only for as long as that work
waits. A cooldown order is due at every tick whose spacing exceeds its interval,
so on a slow-tick city the sweeps saturate the budget permanently and a condition
order whose window is shorter than a full rotation fires only by luck.

## Evidence (maintainer-city, read-only from the graph store and journal)

- `order:*` tracking beads are created in bursts of **exactly 4**, one burst
  every ~18–24 min: 20:04:41, 20:22:21, 20:24:25, 20:42:00, 21:00:11, 21:23:18,
  21:47:10, 22:06:07, 22:25:15, 22:33:59, 22:44:19 … — 12–16 dispatches/hour
  against ~40 enabled orders, i.e. a full rotation every ~3.5 h
  (pr-review-router fired 16:18, 20:24, 23:03). `city.toml` sets no override,
  so the budget is the built-in 4; the tick period on this city is ~20 min, not
  the ~110 s the `max_wakes_per_tick` comment nearby assumes.
- `pr-merge-queue` (trigger=condition, check `pr_merge.py queue-pending`, 2.8 s,
  exit 0 whenever a merge bead is `pr_merge.status=ready`) last fired **14:06Z —
  11 h earlier**. Merge beads for #5604/#5633 were ready 20:25–21:11Z. The ticks
  at **20:42Z and 21:00Z** fell inside that window and each fired four *cooldown*
  orders — beadless-session-reaper, pr-review-label-poll, quota-stall-reset,
  beads-health / cross-rig-deps, gate-sweep, nudge-mail-sweep,
  order-tracking-sweep — while the merge queue's condition was true. Same for the
  21:2x–21:3x window (#5918/#5928/#5929) and the 01:3x window (#5935).
- No gate error, no `order.suppressed` event, no timed-out-check line ever named
  `pr-merge-queue`. It was simply never reached before the budget was spent. The
  starvation was invisible.

Raising `max_dispatches_per_tick` on this city only moves the cliff, which is why
this is an SDK defect rather than a tuning problem.

## The change (`cmd/gc/order_dispatch.go`, `memoryOrderDispatcher.dispatch` phase 2)

Phase 2 is now two passes over the same rotation-ordered candidate list:

1. **Unbudgeted pass** over due condition candidates. Every gate still applies —
   the phase-1 open-tracking gate already ran, the open-work gate runs here, and
   the order self-limits by its own check — but no budget is consulted and no
   rotation cursor moves.
2. **Budgeted pass** over everything else, byte-for-byte the previous semantics:
   same `start`, same `spendDispatchBudget(idx)`, same `return` on exhaustion.
   `maxDispatchesPerTick == 0` still means unbounded.

Both passes call one shared `fireCandidate(...) bool`, so the trigger-env
failure record, the prefetched condition verdict, the lastRun refresh, the
open-work gate and the launch exist exactly once. The open-work gate block moved
into its own `openWorkGateShut` helper to keep both extracted functions under the
repo's complexity threshold.

**Which trigger spelling the branch keys on:** `Order.Trigger == "condition"`,
and that covers both spellings. `gate = "condition"` is folded into `Trigger` by
`orders.orderDecode.normalized()` (`internal/orders/order.go:151`) at scan time
and by `config.OrderOverride.normalizeLegacyAliases()`
(`internal/config/config.go:2173`) at override time, so no `Order` reaches the
dispatcher still carrying a `Gate`. The dispatcher's existing condition branches
(`prefetchConditionResults`, the check-timeout line) key on the same field.

**Observability.** A tick whose budget is spent now logs one grep-able line, in
the shape of the ga-ocypq2 timed-out-check line:

```
gc: order dispatch: per-tick budget 2 spent; the rotation did not reach 3 more order(s) this tick (due-ness not evaluated): cooldown-2, cooldown-3, cooldown-4
```

## Deliberate deviations from the design, and why

- **The line names *unreached* candidates, not a due-list.** The design's draft
  string said "due order(s)". Settling due-ness for the unreached tail would cost
  a per-order last-run fallback query (#3201) and a per-order event-cursor read
  (ga-l7jdg) — exactly the reads the budget exists to avoid — so the line reports
  what the tick already knows for free: the orders that cleared the cheap gates
  and were never reached, and it says so in those words rather than asserting
  deferral. Capped at 8 names plus a count.
- **A trigger-env failure on a condition order stays budgeted.** The design
  listed "trigger env failure" among the logic the unbudgeted pass should run.
  That path writes an *error* tracking bead rather than a dispatch, and
  `TestOrderDispatchTriggerEnvFailuresRespectMaxDispatchesPerTick` exists to keep
  it rationed — a city with 40 misconfigured condition orders would otherwise
  write 40 failure beads per tick. The unbudgeted pass therefore selects on the
  *prefetched passing check* (`conditionResult != nil && Due`), which is the
  literal statement of "work is pending right now".

## Tests — RED → GREEN

New file `cmd/gc/order_dispatch_condition_budget_test.go`, written first.

RED, on the unmodified dispatcher:

```
=== RUN   TestDispatchFiresDueConditionOrderOutsideTheRotationBudget
    order_dispatch_condition_budget_test.go:80: condition order runs after a tick whose budget the sweeps spent = 0, want 1 — the budget starved a due condition order
--- FAIL: TestDispatchFiresDueConditionOrderOutsideTheRotationBudget (0.01s)
=== RUN   TestDispatchConditionOrderStillHonoursOpenTrackingGate
--- PASS: TestDispatchConditionOrd [truncated]

prs.title: feat(beads): proxyendpoint package, doctor endpoint evidence and ping-count shim (native-over-proxy PR1)
prs.author: julianknutsen
prs.request:
PR title: feat(beads): proxyendpoint package, doctor endpoint evidence and ping-count shim (native-over-proxy PR1)

PR description:
PR1 of the dolt-native-over-proxy track (bead `ga-p9iuv.42`). Design:
`~/.cache/gascity-bd/dolt-native-proxy-design-v2.md` §3.2 (discovery), §3.3 step 0
(the cursor gate), §3.4 (idle policy), §5.1 (unit tests), §9 (PR1).

**No behaviour change.** Proxied scopes keep routing to `BdStore`; nothing here
opens the library store, dials on an unproven record, or writes any file bd owns.
What it adds is the ability to *observe* the four preconditions the native path
will need, and the instrument to count what it costs.

## Why

`gc doctor --json` says a proxied city is healthy and nothing else. Whether bd's
proxy is the generation gc last saw, how strong that proof was, whether the
scope's proxy retires itself after 30s of quiet, and whether the database is at
the schema gc's linked library expects are all invisible today — and all four are
preconditions PR2's admission path has to check before it may dial anything.
Separately, gc's bd trace is a partial census of its own subject: the calls it
delegates to the provider script come from a process that records nothing, and
those are exactly the calls the proxied topology added.

## What

**`internal/beads/proxyendpoint`** — gc's one reader of bd's proxy files.
`Read`/`Validate` of the schema-2 `proxy.pid`, with the check bd does not need
because it has an IDENT exchange and gc does not: the record's `root_id` must
equal the id gc recomputes for the root it read it from, so a record copied out
of another workspace is refused rather than dialled. Liveness from a `ProcessTable`
of three injected functions. `IdlePolicy` with bd's three-way sidecar semantics.
A three-outcome `Probe`. `PoolKey` with `SameGeneration`.

Three shapes in it are driven by what "could not tell" costs:

- `Verdict` is an enum, never a bool. `undetermined` (an argv gc could not read)
  and `dead` lead to opposite actions.
- The birth recompute reports `unavailable` explicitly off Linux, and the
  endpoint stays live on argv evidence with `evidence: argv` recorded. Folding
  that into "no match" would retire a live proxy on a hardened kernel.
- `Sidecar.IdleTimeout` is a `*time.Duration`. bd tags the field `omitempty`, so
  a 0 is never written and reads back as absent, and a reader that called absent
  "no timeout" would hold a pool open against a proxy bd retires after 30s.

**The reaper** moves onto the shared parser, decisions byte-identical. It
deliberately does *not* adopt `Validate`: admission refuses what it cannot prove,
protection protects what it cannot rule out, and a legacy or foreign-rooted
record still names a live bd proxy that must not be reaped. A 13-row decision
table fences the move; `TestReaperProofIsNarrowerThanEndpointAdmission` states
the boundary so a later widening has to delete it on purpose.

**Pinned schema cursors** (`SchemaCursorMain = 66`, `SchemaCursorIgnored = 26`)
with a drift test that reads the pinned module's own migration directories out of
the go module cache. beads exports no accessor for either, and a constant only
ever compared against itself would keep reporting "cursors equal, native open
permitted" against a library that had moved on — the first symptom being a
migration the library ran on somebody's shared database. Both lanes, because bd's
shared-store gate consults only the main one and `MigrateUp` then applies pending
ignored-lane migrations without consent.

**`gc doctor --json`** grows `CheckResult.Payload`, projected as `payload` and
omitted for every check that sets none. `beads-store` sets one: the store
selection on every topology, plus on a proxied scope the endpoint record,
verdict, evidence, birth evidence, idle policy and both cursors. Two orderings
are asserted, not just commented: the probe runs only on a `live` verdict (four
unproven-record shapes assert **zero** probes), and the library store is never
opened — the cursors come from two read-only point queries.

**New check `proxied-idle-timeout`** (advisory, warning-not-error, no fix): a
gc-owned proxied scope whose sidecar does not pin its proxy resident. It warns
because the scope works and is only slower than gc's topology intends, and it
offers no fix because the sidecar is bd's file.

**Fork accounting.** The three script exec sites emit `provider-script` records
into the existing JSONL trace; `gc-beads-bd.sh` grows `trace_bd_argv` under
`$GC_BD_TRACE` with a lint that requires it before *every* bd fork by shape;
`test/acceptance/helpers` gets a recording `BD_BIN` shim that records and then
execs the pinned bd. `TestBeadsProxiedDefault` wires it and asserts the
instrument before anything is built on it — a count taken through a shim nothing
forks is zero by construction.

## Finding: gc's init needs no change (design §3.4 / U19)

The design asks whether gc's own init must be changed to write `idle_timeout: -1`.
It must not, and already does not, on three independent sources:

1. beads v1.3.0 `cmd/bd/init.go:438,514-523` rewrites an *explicitly set*
   `--proxied-server-idle-timeout 0` to `proxy.IdleTimeoutNever` (`-1ns`) before
   persisting, and rejects a negative value on the CLI outright — so passing `0`
   is the only way to ask for never.
2. `gc-beads-bd.sh:2755,3646` already passes exactly that flag at both init sites
   (and `initDefaultRigBdStore` at the third).
3. The matrix already asserts the result on real cities
   (`beads_proxied_default_test.go` `idle_timeout == -1`,
   `helpers/beads_topology.go` `IdleTimeout: -1`).

What was missing was a check that says so out loud — which is what
`proxied-idle-timeout` adds. (`bd migrate from-server-to-proxied-server` with the
flag omitted persists 0 → absent → 30s, which is the operator-default shape the
check warns about.)

## Bug found while writing the shim

The recording format was line-oriented at first, which split any invocation whose
argv contained a newline [truncated]

prs.title: fix(test/doctor): read bd's stdout, not its merged stderr (ga-x5wacn)
prs.author: quad341
prs.request:
PR title: fix(test/doctor): read bd's stdout, not its merged stderr (ga-x5wacn)

PR description:
Fixes the `internal/doctor` failure that has been blocking the local push gate fleet-wide (ga-x5wacn).

## Symptom

`TestCustomTypesCheck_ServerBackedStoreIgnoresAmbientEndpoint` fails with:

```
parsing bd config get output: invalid character '/' after top-level value
```

Near-deterministic under `make test-fast-parallel` (reported 7/7 across two
unrelated diffs in a single day, by three independent sessions), and a clean
pass in isolation every time. That split is what made it look like
un-actionable fleet contention, and it was triaged that way — the standing
guidance had become "don't investigate this, degrade gracefully and push
without it".

## Root cause

Not contention corrupting bd's JSON, which is what the symptom suggests and
what the bead originally recorded. The test ran bd through
`cmd.CombinedOutput()` and handed the **merged** buffer to a strict
`json.Unmarshal`. bd reports diagnostics on stderr through the standard `log`
package, whose prefix is a bare `2026/09/19 18:23:29 ` timestamp. Merged ahead
of the JSON document, `json.Unmarshal` reads `2026` as a complete top-level
number and then fails on the `/`.

## Why this is the cause, and not the other theory

**The error text is a fingerprint.** Of the plausible ways a concurrent bd
could corrupt the document itself — truncation at either end, interleaved
duplicate, NUL injection, partial write, empty output, foreign ASCII prefix —
none produces this message; each produces a visibly different one
(`unexpected end of JSON input`, `invalid character 'x' looking for beginning
of value`, and so on). Only a leading `<digits>/` sequence, i.e. a Go log
timestamp, produces `invalid character '/' after top-level value`. Random
corruption also would not reproduce identically across every report.

**It explains the composition-dependence.** bd emits nothing on stderr at
idle (measured: 0 bytes), so the test passes standalone. Under parallel load
the Dolt circuit breaker trips and logs its recovery line on exactly the path
where the command still *succeeds* — bd exits 0 with valid JSON on stdout and
a timestamped line on stderr. The installed bd binary does contain that
emitter (`[circuit-breaker] %s:%d/%s: open `, `active probe succeeded`). So
"passes in isolation" was never evidence against this bug; it is a predicted
symptom of it.

**Production was already immune, deliberately.** `checks_custom_types.go`
uses `cmd.Output()` on this same path. The test was the lone outlier, so
`gc doctor` itself was never affected — this is a test-only defect.

## The change

One call: `cmd.CombinedOutput()` → `cmd.Output()`, matching production.

stderr is not discarded. `Output` leaves it on `*exec.ExitError`, so
`mustRunBD` now reports **both** streams on failure — strictly more
diagnostic detail than the merged form gave, not less.

The parse is guarded by a new case in the existing `TestParseCustomTypesJSON`
table asserting that a stderr-prefixed document is still *rejected* rather
than skipped. Tolerating a prefix there would mask genuine corruption; the
caller is what must not merge the streams.

## Deliberately out of scope

- The sibling `CombinedOutput` further up the same file is left alone: that
  loop scans **both** streams for leaked shared-server messages, so merging is
  correct there.
- A repo-wide scan found one undefended instance of the same pattern on a real
  `bd` invocation (`cmd/gc/beads_provider_lifecycle_test.go`) and one already
  defended by hand (`cmd/gc/cmd_bd_test.go`'s `parseCreatedBeadID`, which skips
  to the first `{`). Filed separately rather than mixed into this P1 unblock.

## Verification

- Target test passes in isolation (9.26s, matching the ~7.6s documented
  baseline).
- **Passed under the composition that reproduced the bug**: in a full
  `make test-fast-parallel` push gate, `internal/doctor` came back
  `ok ... 44.292s` — a genuinely contended run, not an accidentally quiet one.
- `TestParseCustomTypesJSON` green including the new case.
- `go vet ./internal/doctor/` clean; pre-commit `lint-changed` 0 issues.
- `internal/testpolicy/resourcecensus` green: the fix adds no subprocess call
  sites, so the untagged subprocess ratchet stays flat.

prs.title: chore(beads): post-merge follow-ups for the v1.3.0 pin (perm preservation, rc.2 strings)
prs.author: julianknutsen
prs.request:
PR title: chore(beads): post-merge follow-ups for the v1.3.0 pin (perm preservation, rc.2 strings)

PR description:
Post-merge follow-ups for #6273, now that `main` pins the beads **v1.3.0 tag**
(`deps.env` `BD_CURRENT_VERSION=v1.3.0` / `BD_CURRENT_REF=f45b249ce…`, `go.mod`
`github.com/steveyegge/beads v1.3.0`). There is no pin bump here — this is the
cleanup the pin left behind, plus the two low findings from the round-5 delta
review of #6273.

Three commits, one per item.

---

## 1. Keep bd's `0600` mode when canonicalising `.beads` files

`103d72428e` — `internal/beads/contract/files.go`

#6273 moved the four canonical writers from `fs.WriteFile` to
`fsys.WriteFileAtomic`. `WriteFile`'s perm argument only applies **on create**,
so an existing file kept whatever mode its owner chose. `WriteFileAtomic`
publishes a fresh inode by rename and chmods it to the perm it was handed, so
it stamps the mode unconditionally.

bd creates both `.beads/config.yaml` and `.beads/metadata.json` `0600`
(`cmd/bd/init_templates.go`, `internal/configfile/configfile.go`) and re-saves
`metadata.json` `0600` partway through `bd migrate`. Since the atomic switch,
every boot-door canonicalisation, every `gc rig set-endpoint` and every
migrate-proxied turn widened a bd-created scope's files to `0644`.

Neither file holds a secret today (`config.yaml` records only
`dolt_server_user`; no password or token keys), so this is a mode-preservation
regression rather than an exposure — but gc should not silently relax a mode
another owner chose.

New `canonicalScopeFilePerm(fs, path)` stats the target and reuses its mode
when it is an existing regular file, falling back to gc's own `0644` only when
the file does not exist yet. Wired into all four writers:
`SetMetadataDoltDataDir`, `EnsureCanonicalConfig`, `EnsureCanonicalMetadata`,
`ensureCanonicalConfigFallback`.

**Tests** (`files_atomic_write_test.go`):

- `TestCanonicalWritersPreserveAnExistingRestrictiveMode` — seeds both files
  `0600` and drives all four writers, asserting `0600` survives. The fourth row
  seeds malformed YAML so `EnsureCanonicalConfig` falls through to
  `ensureCanonicalConfigFallback`, which is otherwise unreachable from a table
  (confirmed by coverage: `files.go:863` hit).
- `TestCanonicalMetadataWriterUsesTheDefaultModeForANewFile` — pins the create
  case at `0644`, so the fallback default cannot be dropped.

Fail-before verified: with the four call sites reverted to a literal `0o644`,
all four subtests fail with `the canonical write widened … to 0644, want 0600`.

## 2. A published managed Dolt runtime is not bd's upstream

`b4c85656ca` — `cmd/gc/beads_scope_ownership.go`

`scopeIsBdOwnedDirectExternal` decides whether gc leaves a scope's canonical
files alone and declines the managed Dolt lifecycle. Its only discriminator
between "bd's foreign upstream" and "gc's own managed server" is the host in
bd's persisted binding, compared against `managedCityHost()` — which reads
`GC_DOLT_HOST` from the **live** environment.

That leaves a drift case with three preconditions:

1. `.beads/config.yaml` is not gc-authoritative — a city last booted before
   `gc.endpoint_origin` existed, or one whose config was restored to bd's
   `issue_prefix:` template;
2. `metadata.json` records a non-loopback `dolt_server_host` — reachable when
   gc ran `bd init` under a non-local `GC_DOLT_HOST`;
3. the booting gc has `GC_DOLT_HOST` unset or pointing elsewhere.

Then gc reads its own server as bd's upstream: the boot door stops stamping
`managed_city`, `managedDoltLifecycleOwned` answers false, the lifecycle skips
`ensureBeadsProvider`, and the resolver falls to the stale `host:port` as
External. The failure is loud, but clearing it needs a hand-edited
`config.yaml` or a restored `GC_DOLT_HOST`.

Answer false when a Dolt runtime publication exists for the city under
`.gc/runtime/packs/dolt` — the same "a prior gc runtime publication is evidence
of the direct managed lifecycle" rule `scopeUsesProxiedDoltMode` already
applies, and the one piece of evidence on disk only gc writes. Existence is the
whole signal; the record is never read, since state left behind by a Dolt that
died uncleanly is still proof of who owns the lifecycle.

Classification is untouched everywhere else: the predicate's other arms, the
three `providerOwnedScopeState` arms, and the journaled/proxied paths
classified before it all behave as before.

**Tests:** `TestScopeIsBdOwnedDirectExternal` — a three-row table pinning the
bare M3b shape as bd-owned and each of the two publication paths as not. Both
publication rows fail before the fix with `= true, want false`.
`TestBootCanonicalizationKeepsBdsUpstream*`, `TestScopeCarries*`,
`TestProviderOwnership*` and `TestBeadsCityEndpointRefuses*` re-run green.

### Review follow-up: the guard is per-scope, not city-level (`1cfb1c060b`)

Review found the first cut of this commit **high**, and it was right. Answering
false on a city-level publication re-introduced R1-F1 for rigs — the split
brain `2a615a90f9` fixed.

`startBeadsLifecycle` raises the city's own provider
(`beads_provider_lifecycle.go:248-262`), publishing `dolt-state.json` at
`:1588`, **before** it reaches the rig loop at `:277`. So by the time any rig is
classified the publication always exists. An un-journaled bd-owned
direct-external rig on any gc-managed city therefore answered false,
`normalizeCanonicalBdScopeFilesForInit` stamped `gc.endpoint_origin:
inherited_city` into bd's `config.yaml`, and `bd init` ran for the rig against
gc's server — creating an empty database there while `bd` in the rig still
reached the real upstream. Once that marker exists
`ResolveDoltConnectionTarget` skips the binding (`connection.go:694-699`), so
the split is permanent. Nor was it bounded by Dolt being live: a clean
`gc stop` rewrites `dolt-provider-state.json` with `running:false` rather than
removing it (`gc-beads-bd.sh:2559`).

prs.author: quad341
prs.request:
PR title: perf(gc): decline the revision snapshot in the hosted-credential probe (ga-s3cnmy)

PR description:
## What

`citySelectsHostedBeadsCredentialProvider` (`cmd/gc/bd_env.go`) loads `city.toml`
to read one boolean off the storage binding and discards the Provenance on the
same line. It never computes a `config.Revision()`, so it can never observe the
load-time revision snapshot — but the default load builds one anyway, and
building it reads and SHA-256s **every file of every pack directory,
recursively** (`captureRevisionSnapshot` → `packContentHashRecursive`, which
`internal/config/revision.go` calls with `useCache=false`).

That probe runs on the env/runner construction path for **every `bd`
subprocess** — and twice per invocation, from both `applyHostedBeadsCredentialEnv`
(`:614`) and `beadsCommandRunnerForHostedCity` (`:660`).

This passes `config.LoadOptions{SkipRevisionSnapshot: true}` there, and adds a
source-level guard test.

## Why — measured, not inferred (ga-s3cnmy)

Investigating a reconcile tick of 5.5–8 min on the `gc-management` controller
(deployed `gc ca73feb679`, pid 2465414, 2026-09-16).

**The controller is CPU-bound on its own work, not waiting on `bd`.**
`/proc/<pid>/stat` over one 45 s window — fields 14/15 are the process's own
utime/stime, 16/17 its reaped children's:

| | cpu-seconds in 45 s |
|---|---|
| controller's own | **129.75** (288% of a core) |
| every child process combined (`bd`, `ps`, …) | **24.17** (50% of a core) |

`perf record -F 199 --call-graph=fp`, two independent captures in **different**
tick phases (60 s/18200 samples; 45 s/31781 samples), inclusive:

| symbol | capture 1 | capture 2 |
|---|---|---|
| `config.LoadWithIncludesOptions` | 72.89% | 72.74% |
| `citySelectsHostedBeadsCredentialProvider` | 58.76% | 58.19% |
| `captureRevisionSnapshot` / `packContentHashRecursive` | 29.16% / 29.02% | |
| `sha256.blockSHANI` (self) | 15.92% | 15.40% |
| BurntSushi/toml lexer+parser (self, summed) | ~13.2% | ~12.4% |

Caller histogram for `LoadWithIncludesOptions`:
`citySelectsHostedBeadsCredentialProvider` 12998 samples (80.4%),
`loadPrematerializedCityConfig` 3170 (19.6%).

Per-load cost against this city's real `city.toml` (n=8, warmed):

| | per call |
|---|---|
| default (as called before) | **94.55 ms** |
| `SkipRevisionSnapshot: true` | **38.77 ms** (−59%) |

#4917 added `SkipRevisionSnapshot` for exactly this caller shape and scoped its
guard test to `cmd_agent.go`, saying in the test's own comment that the other
Provenance-discarding call sites were out of scope "for later". This is one of
those, and it is the hottest one in the controller.

## Safety

`LoadWithIncludes` is literally `LoadWithIncludesOptions(fs, path, LoadOptions{})`,
and `SkipRevisionSnapshot` is read in exactly one place (`compose.go:863`), gating
only `prov.captureRevisionSnapshot(...)`. The returned `*City` is unchanged, and
this caller discards the Provenance. No value can differ.

## Why a source-level guard test

Same reason `TestCityConfigLoadersDeclineTheRevisionSnapshot` is source-level:
reverting to the default returns an identical config and passes every functional
test. Nothing fails — it only gets slower, which is precisely the regression a
suite does not otherwise catch. Verified RED before the change, GREEN after.

## Scope — what this does NOT fix

Three larger findings from the same investigation are recorded on `ga-s3cnmy`
and each needs its own bead:

1. The remaining ~39 ms/load is `expandPacks` + TOML parse, still paid per `bd`
   subprocess. The real fix is memoizing the boolean itself across its 6
   non-test call sites, which needs an invalidation story for runtime config
   reload — an architecture call.
2. `liveWorkAssignmentAssigneeMatches` (`cmd/gc/work_assignment.go:334`) issues a
   full `List(Status, Live, TierBoth)` and linear-scans it to check **one** bead's
   assignee. It sits in a release path that clears assignees, so it is not a
   mechanical edit.
3. `CachingStore.refreshCachedBeads` re-`Get`s every cached-but-absent bead on
   every `Live` list and never converges — measured 3,227 `bd show` calls over
   893 distinct ids in 11 minutes, most re-fetched 3–6×.

This is also **not** a `release_orphaned_pool_assignments`-specific bug: capture 2
landed in a different phase (`runDetachedOrphanBackstop`) and shows the same
pathology at the same percentages. Every phase issuing a `Live` list pays it.

## Caveat

The improvement is measured at the config-load layer and by perf attribution, not
as a before/after tick time on a rebuilt controller — that needs a `gc` deploy,
and the deploy point is currently frozen behind the reaper type-scope guard
(`9296d22db8` is an ancestor of `origin/main` but not of the deployed
`ca73feb679`). Re-run `supbd-sampler.sh` at its own 200 ms cadence plus one perf
capture after the next deploy to confirm the magnitude.
